title: fix(console): return packages/core to the framework chunk by grouping rule, and pin chunk membership
body:
Part of #9345 — route B, director seat decision batch 128, item 2. Six of the card's seven acceptance criteria are met on the merged head. Criterion 3 is only partly met: its clause "`framework` back above its baseline" is not met, because `framework` reads 70,020 gzipped bytes against its 72,245 baseline. It cannot be met here without undoing objectui#10082's ruled split or re-pinning a baseline, and both are forbidden. The criteria and their readings are below.

Round 3 of this pull request, by session `session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`, on the claim holder's order (card comments `5825422033` and `5826915183`). This round merges `main` in, keeps both rulings, and declares objectui#10082's `packages/types` split in the membership pin, exactly. Every table below was re-measured on the merged head `48387d4d1`, which is `main` at `2a943bf0c` plus this branch. Readings from earlier rounds are kept at the end, labelled with the tree they were taken on.

---

## 1. The merge — both rulings kept

- The previous round's worktree held an uncommitted merge of `ff14e29b5`, and `main` had since moved 26 commits, some of them in `packages/core` and `packages/types`. Those are the packages the pin names, so measuring on the stale merge would have described a tree that does not exist.
- Before aborting, the in-progress merge was checked for manual work, and it held none:
  - Every stage-0 index entry equalled a clean `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the same two commits.
  - The three conflicted files differed from that output only in the conflict-marker label.
- It was aborted, and `main` was merged again at `2a943bf0c`, pinned by SHA into a ref this round named itself. The result is merge commit `0933e6f7f`. There was no rebase and no force-push.
- Three conflicts, each resolved to keep both sides:
  - `apps/console/vite.config.ts` carries this branch's `includeDependenciesRecursively: false` on `data-adapter` (priority 84) **and** objectui#10082's `types-zod` group at priority 82 with its own `includeDependenciesRecursively: false`. `framework` stays at 80.
  - `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` carries the membership half **and** `main`'s RETIRED block for the exhausted-headroom leg (objectui#10148, #10151). That leg no longer exists on `main`. The sensitivity half that remains passes on every leg below.
  - `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` uses this branch's group parse, which captures the options tail. That parse covers `main`'s shorter tail and still sees `types-zod`.
- No lockfile or generated file conflicted, and this branch changes no manifest, so nothing needed regenerating.

## 2. The `packages/types` split, declared exactly

Before this round the pin said "`packages/types` lands WHOLLY in `framework`". After objectui#10082 that is false by ruling. This round neither drops the package nor loosens the claim. It declares the exception:

```js
export const PER_CHUNK_MEMBERSHIP_CARVE_OUTS = Object.freeze({
  types: Object.freeze([Object.freeze({ subtree: 'src/zod', chunk: 'types-zod' })]),
});
```

**How a carved package is judged.** A carved package is judged per DIRECTORY rather than per package:
- every module under `packages/types/src/zod` must land in `types-zod`;
- every other module of `packages/types` must land in `framework`;
- nothing may land anywhere else;
- each side must hold at least one module.

The rule stays EXACT: one stray module is a finding, named by its directory. The per-directory counts are what tell the healthy split apart from the failure objectui#10082 met on its first build, where shared `src/` neighbours were absorbed into `types-zod` along an import. A per-package count reads those two cases identically.

**The gate's rules still hold.**
- The declaration keys stay limited to chunks that carry a ceiling.
- A carve-out's destination is not a key. It may carry no ceiling only while it is ABSENT from the same build's eager closure, which the gate reads from `eager-closure.json`. A carve-out into an unbudgeted EAGER chunk is refused as an error, because that is objectui#9345's own incident written down as a ruling. That is also why no carve-out can say "any chunk".
- A unit cross-check against the console config requires all of the following:
  - the carve-out group's own test matches the subtree;
  - the declared chunk's test also matches the subtree;
  - the carve-out group's test MISSES the rest of the package (the must-miss control);
  - the carve-out group outranks the declared chunk;
  - the carve-out group declares `includeDependenciesRecursively: false`.

**Refused as errors, never passed:**
- nested carve-outs;
- a carve-out into the package's own chunk;
- a carve-out of an undeclared package;
- a malformed subtree;
- a carve-out with an unreadable eager closure;
- a subtree or remainder that holds nothing;
- directory counts that do not add up to the package counts.

**The emitter.** `chunk-membership.json` goes to v2 and adds `directories`, keyed package, then package-relative directory, then chunk, then count. A stale v1 artifact is therefore refused. The emitter reads no declaration.

## 3. Membership, from a real build: before and after this PR's config, same merged tree

⚠️ Built first. The console's dependency closure was built with `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...' --concurrency=2`: 34 of 34 tasks, 0 cached, exit 0. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` ran for each leg. The BEFORE leg is the merged tree with `data-adapter`'s narrowing deleted. That is `main`'s own grouping rule, with this branch's emitter present so the leg can be read. Attribution comes from each emitted chunk's own `modules`, never from the config.

| package | BEFORE (flag removed) | AFTER (`48387d4d1`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `packages/core` | 52 in `data-adapter`, 26 in `framework` | **78 in `framework`** |
| `packages/types`, outside `src/zod` | 3 in `data-adapter`, 10 in `framework` | **13 in `framework`** |
| `packages/types/src/zod` | 9 in `types-zod` | 9 in `types-zod` |
| `packages/react` | 65 in `framework` | 65 in `framework` |
| `packages/data-objectstack` | 8 in `data-adapter` | 8 in `data-adapter` |
| `packages/components` / `fields` | 205 / 81 in `ui-components` | 205 / 81 in `ui-components` |

After the repair, `data-adapter` holds exactly its declared regex and nothing else. On this tree the defect reaches 52 of `packages/core`'s 78 modules, where earlier rounds saw 92 of 92. `main` has changed underneath:
- objectui#9492 landed as `5e0b22c2c`. At `2a943bf0c` the grep for its cast reads 0, while a control grep finds the dynamic import it narrowed still present.
- Other commits changed `packages/core` itself.

⚠️ Which of these accounts for the smaller count was not measured separately. The rule that moves the modules is the same, and firing control A below shows it.

## 4. Bytes, same two legs (gzipped at zlib's default level, as the emitter weighs them)

| chunk | BEFORE | AFTER | delta |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `framework` (eager, ceiling 100,000) | 42,997 | **70,020** | +27,023 |
| `data-adapter` (eager, no ceiling) | 46,837 | **19,098** | −27,739 |
| `framework` + `data-adapter` | 89,834 | 89,118 | −716 |
| `types-zod` (lazy, not in the closure) | 28,733 | 28,731 | −2 |
| whole eager closure | 3,118,280 | 3,117,418 | −862 |
| eager chunks / total | 329 / 2310 | 329 / 2310 | 0 |

- The bytes were always downloaded, because `data-adapter` is in the eager closure. This is a re-attribution, not a payload change.
- `data-adapter` returns to the neighbourhood of the 19.6 K that the gate's exemption rests on, as the ruling's point 3 required.
- `framework` sits under its ceiling with 29.3 KB of headroom.
- Every figure above was read twice and agreed: `eager-closure.json`'s own `gzipBytes`, and a re-gzip of the file on disk.
- The AFTER leg was built twice, once before the firing control and once after its restore. Both builds were real `vite build` runs, not cache restores, and their `eager-closure.json` and `chunk-membership.json` are byte-identical.

`pnpm check:eager-closure` on the AFTER build exits **0**, and every half is green:
- the aggregate closure, at 3044.4 KB against 3104.5 KB;
- all four per-chunk ceilings;
- membership: "5 budgeted package(s) each landed exactly where declared", naming `packages/types` as "13 modules in `framework` and its `src/zod` subtree 9 in `types-zod`, exactly";
- the sensitivity half, with all five ceilings within one regression.

The freshness half is not applicable to a local run. `check:eager-locale-catalogues` exits 0. ⛔ No ceiling, baseline or exemption constant moved.

## 5. Firing controls, proven on disk

Every mutation below went through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode:
- the anchor must hit exactly once;
- the blob change is verified on disk;
- a restore is armed on EXIT, INT and TERM against the absolute path;
- after the restore, a separate check requires the worktree blob to equal `HEAD`'s and `git diff HEAD` to be empty.

A first attempt at leg A used a replacement that contained its own anchor, so the tool refused it as a no-op before anything was built. It was re-run in delete mode, which is the reading below.

**A. The defect itself: `data-adapter`'s narrowing deleted, then a rebuild.**
- The blob changed from `b9afdeae39ed` to `15c4e3fe6fbd`.
- `check:eager-closure` exited **1**. Every byte ceiling was green, with `framework` at 42.0 KB and 55.7 KB of apparent headroom. The membership half fired:

  ```
  ❌ `packages/core` is declared in `framework` but 52 in `data-adapter` (26 of its 78 modules landed in `framework`)
  ❌ `packages/types` is declared in `framework` with its `src/zod` subtree -> `types-zod`, but `packages/types/src` 3 in `data-adapter` (declared `framework`)
  ```

- The static unit pin fired too: 1 failed of 177, namely "narrows `data-adapter` to its own regex".
- Restore: the blob returned to `b9afdeae39ed`, equal to `HEAD`, and `git diff HEAD` was empty.
- A rebuild then exited 0 with membership `pass`.

**B. The split declaration, mis-declared.** Each case below ran against the real AFTER build's artifacts, and each was restored with the same proof.

| mutation of `PER_CHUNK_MEMBERSHIP_CARVE_OUTS` | `check:eager-closure` | what it printed | unit file |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| none (control) | exit 0 | membership `pass` | 177 passed |
| carve-out deleted (the old wholesale pin) | exit **1** | `packages/types` is declared in `framework` but 9 in `types-zod` | 13 failed |
| chunk pointed at `plugin-map` | exit **1** | `packages/types/src/zod` 9 in `types-zod` (declared `plugin-map`) | 8 failed |
| chunk pointed at `data-adapter` (eager, no ceiling) | exit **2** | carved into `data-adapter`, which is in the EAGER closure and carries no ceiling | 17 failed |

**Lint was narrowed, and the narrowing is declared.** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` ran over all five lintable files in this diff: four from the root config, and `apps/console/vite.config.ts` from its package. Result: 0 errors and 0 warnings. The file count comes from the JSON output. The `.yml` file is outside eslint's population. A file this diff does not touch cannot change its verdict, for two reasons:
- `eslint.config.js` configures no `projectService` or `parserOptions` (grep exit 1; control grep for `rules` exit 0), so type-aware linting is off.
- No rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem (grep exit 1; control grep exit 0 with 11 hits).

Exit codes were captured by redirecting to a file and then reading the code, never across a pipe.

**NOT MEASURED:**
- `check:docs-route-closure`: it needs `apps/site`'s build, and nothing here reaches it. Its tests ran inside `scripts/`.
- The freshness half: it needs the `pull_request` merge-ref environment.
- The package size report: CI builds `./packages/*`, while this round built the console's dependency closure.

`gates_weakened:` **NONE.** The `packages/types` assertion is replaced by an exact split. The only modules it admits outside `framework` are the ruled subtree, and it holds that subtree to one chunk. The carve-out's destination must stay out of the eager closure, and it is refused as an error the moment it does not. No assertion was deleted and none was given headroom.

## 7. #9345's acceptance criteria, read on the merged head

Quoted from the card's dispatch (comment `5662155820`):

1. *"The rolldown rule that re-attributed the subgraph is named, with the reading that identifies it."* ✅ `CodeSplittingGroup.includeDependenciesRecursively`, default `true`. Firing control A reproduces it on today's tree.
2. *"`packages/core` lands in `framework` after a real build, shown by the emitted chunk's own module list."* ✅ 78 in `framework` and 0 anywhere else, from `chunk-membership.json`, which is built from `output.modules`.
3. *"The byte table re-measured after the repair: `framework` back above its baseline and under its ceiling, `data-adapter` back down."* ⚠️ **Partly met.**
   - Under its ceiling: ✅ 70,020 of 100,000.
   - `data-adapter` back down: ✅ 46,837 → 19,098.
   - Back above its baseline: ❌ 70,020 against 72,245, which is 2,225 below. The cause is a ruled change, not this branch: objectui#10082 moved the 28,731-byte `src/zod` subtree out of `framework` into a lazy chunk, and the 72,245 baseline was measured on `3f775eeb8` with those validators inside. Counting the split's two chunks together gives 98,751, but that is not the criterion's measure, and it is shown only to explain the gap.
4. *"The membership pin has a firing control."* ✅ Section 5, A and B.
5. *"`gates_weakened:` NONE, or name exactly what and why."* ✅ Section 6.
6. *"Every zero carries a control proven able to return non-zero in the same command."* ✅ Each zero reading carries its control:
   - the restore proofs pair with a mutated blob;
   - the lint greps pair with control greps;
   - the changeset zero pairs with the mutation in section 8;
   - the eager-report and on-disk gzip figures agree.
7. *"A changeset, or a measured statement that none is owed."* ✅ Section 8.

⇒ this is `Part of`. The unmet clause of criterion 3 needs one of two dispositions from the seat or the maintainer:
- retire the card when this merges, as superseded by objectui#10082's ruled split; or
- carry the clause to the follow-up card objectui#10085 on the `framework` ceiling, which is where `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE.framework` would be revisited.

⛔ This round moves neither constant.

The console build config is not published source under that script's rule. This round's card claim carries no `Clause-②:` line, so none is written here.
